criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`: it passes, with new tests showing the checks step receives a CI source backed by the platform and not `NoCi`. They also show the candidate commit is pushed before CI is read, the same SHA is used for both, and the wait uses the configured bound rather than one poll.
criteria.evidence: I ran 13 matching tests and all passed. Athena reports that the full `cargo test --locked` passed with 877 tests. `pushed_a_green_run_for_the_sha_replaces_the_local_checks` shows the push comes before the read and both use the same SHA (log == [push SHA, read SHA]). `pushed_waits_for_the_configured_bound...` shows reads == polls, but only for a test-only `BOUND` (4 polls) passed directly to `run_pushed`. No test exercises the checks step in run.rs. Nothing shows that it builds a `GhClient` rather than using `NoCi`, or that it passes `CI_WAIT`. `the_ci_wait_bound_is_more_than_one_poll` only checks the constant's value. The run.rs wiring at lines 1015-1051 is not tested.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: tests with fake push and CI sources show a green CI run for the candidate SHA means no local check runs and the check records say they came from CI with the run address. A run for another SHA, a missing run after the bounded wait, and a push failure each run the three checks locally exactly once. A red run fails and does not run locally.
criteria.evidence: These tests passed: pushed_a_green_run_for_the_sha_replaces_the_local_checks (ran empty, from_ci, note contains runs/5), pushed_a_run_for_another_sha_runs_locally_once, pushed_waits_for_the_configured_bound_and_then_runs_locally_once, pushed_a_failed_push_reads_no_ci_and_runs_locally_once (each ran == [fmt, clippy, test]), and pushed_a_red_run_fails_and_does_not_run_locally.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: both are clean.
criteria.evidence: Both exited cleanly with no output or warnings.

criteria.criterion: The push goes through the existing guarded push path (`check_push`, the work branch only). No new push mechanism is added, and nothing is pushed to the default branch.
criteria.evidence: `gh::push_work_branch` (gh.rs:1042-1064) reads the remote head, calls `check_push` with allowed_branch = branch = work_branch(job), then calls `Remote::push`. run.rs uses `GitRemote` on origin. No other branch is named.

criteria.criterion: The wait bound is a named, documented value (a constant or a config field) with a stated basis, and the run output says whether the checks came from CI or ran locally. If `athena.toml` gets a field, it is named and the schema/load tests are updated.
criteria.evidence: `routing::CI_WAIT` has a doc comment giving its basis (the section 1 figure of about 6 minutes, said to be unmeasured) and saying it is to be revised with section 9 data. `run_pushed` reports 'ci         checks came from CI: <note with run URL>' or 'ci         checks ran locally' through ctx.ui.line. No athena.toml field was added.

criteria.criterion: docs/design/ci-routing.md section 10 items 4 and 5 are updated: the push and wait are no longer listed as 'not done'. The verifier's reuse is still listed as not done, and no speedup is claimed without a measurement.
criteria.evidence: The diff of ci-routing.md updates item 4 (the push and wait are described as done; the verifier's input and a measured bound are not done; 'No speedup is claimed or measured') and item 5 (the verifier's reuse statement is still not done).

criteria.criterion: The `fmt`, `clippy` and `test` checks are not changed in definition. The verifier's input and prompts are not changed.
criteria.evidence: The diff touches only gh.rs, routing.rs, run.rs, ci-routing.md and CHANGELOG.md. It changes no check specs, athena.toml, verify.rs or prompts.

findings.summary: Pushing the candidate to `athena/<job>` makes the later `athena land --pr` push of that job refused as not a fast-forward.
findings.evidence: The candidate commit's parent is the base `p` (run.rs:906; its message says 'Not on any branch; landing builds its own commit'). The landed commit is built with `build_commit(&tree, &head, ...)` (run.rs:1689/1896), so its parent is the local head and it does not descend from the candidate. When no PR link exists, `land_pr` calls `publish`, which runs `check_push` with the remote head of `athena/<job>`. After this change, that remote head is the candidate commit, which is not an ancestor of the landed commit, so the guard refuses the push (see pr::tests::the_guard_refuses_a_non_fast_forward_push). Landing by pull request would therefore fail for every job whose candidate was pushed. No test covers a job run followed by `land --pr`. The out-of-scope list allows reusing landing's push, but not breaking it.

findings.summary: No test covers the run.rs wiring: nothing shows that the checks step gets a platform-backed source and `CI_WAIT` rather than `NoCi` with one poll.
findings.evidence: The new tests call `routing::run_pushed` directly with fake sources and a test-only `BOUND`. If run.rs went back to `NoCi` or one poll, no test would fail. This is part of criterion 1.

findings.summary: The candidate commit message still says 'Not on any branch', but the commit is now pushed to a branch.
findings.evidence: The message reads "Candidate for job {id}\n\nNot on any branch; landing builds its own commit.", but the change now pushes that commit to athena/<job>.

findings.summary: When the push succeeds but CI never reports, every job waits about 20 minutes before running the checks locally.
findings.evidence: CI_WAIT is 60 polls × 20 s. If the push succeeds but no run appears (for example, Actions is disabled), the job pays about 20 minutes plus the local run. The bound is documented as conservative, so this is a design trade-off, not a criterion violation.

summary: The change adds `routing::run_pushed`, `CI_WAIT` (60 reads, 20 s apart) and `gh::push_work_branch`. The job run now pushes the candidate commit to `athena/<job>` and reads CI through `GhClient`. The fake-source tests for green, red, other-SHA, missing-run, failed-push and build cases pass, and fmt and clippy are clean. The verdict is fail for two reasons. First, the change breaks landing. After the job run, the work branch holds the candidate commit. But `athena land --pr` builds its landed commit on the local head, not on the candidate, and its first push (`publish`) goes through `check_push`, which refuses any push that is not a fast-forward. Every job whose candidate was pushed would therefore be refused when it lands as a pull request, and nothing in the change handles this or tests it. Second, nothing tests the run.rs wiring: no test shows that the real checks step passes a platform-backed source and `CI_WAIT`. The new tests only call `run_pushed` with fakes and a test-only bound.
